The '''2020–21 [[Coupe de France]]''' was the 104th season of the main football cup competition of [[Football in France|France]]. The competition was organised by the [[French Football Federation]] (FFF) and is normally open to all clubs in [[Football in France|French football]], as well as clubs from the [[Overseas France|overseas departments and territories]] ([[Guadeloupe]], [[French Guiana]], [[Martinique]], [[Mayotte]], [[New Caledonia]], [[French Polynesia|Tahiti]], [[Réunion]], [[Collectivity of Saint Martin|Saint Martin]], and [[Saint Pierre and Miquelon]]). Due to the [[travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]], the club from Saint Pierre and Miquelon did not progress beyond the second round{{Efn|By regulation, the winning club of second round of the [[2020–21 Coupe de France preliminary rounds, Overseas departments and territories#Saint Pierre and Miquelon|Saint Pierre and Miquelon regional draw]] qualify for the third round of Pays de la Loire regional draw; but travel restrictions prevented the team from Saint Pierre and Miquelon making the trip.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.footamateur.fr/coupe-de-france-le-representant-de-saint-pierre-et-miquelon-ne-se-deplacera-pas/|title=Coupe de France. Le représentant de Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon ne se déplacera pas|language=fr|publisher=footamateur.fr|date=8 September 2020|access-date=20 April 2021}}</ref>|name=|group=note}} and qualifying clubs from New Caledonia and Tahiti did not participate.

The competition was paused on 28 October 2020, when France entered a second period of lockdown due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in France|COVID-19 pandemic]]. On 17 December, the FFF announced a new format to allow the competition to complete. On 22 December, the FFF announced a plan to resume the competition from 31 January 2021.

On 19 January 2021, the FFF produced a new calendar for the amateur path and the final stages.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.footamateur.fr/coupe-de-france-le-protocole-de-reprise-pour-les-clubs-amateurs/|title=Coupe de France: Le protocole de reprise pour les clubs amateurs |publisher=footamateur.fr |language=fr|date=19 January 2021|access-date=25 May 2021}}</ref>

[[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] were the defending champions, and they won a record fourteenth title with a 2–0 win over [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]] in the [[2021 Coupe de France Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/57177755|title=Monaco 0–2 Paris Saint-Germain: PSG win sixth French Cup in seven years|website=BBC Sport|date=19 May 2021|access-date=19 May 2021}}</ref>

==Dates==

Dates for the first two qualifying round were set by the individual Regional leagues. The original calendar had the remaining qualifying rounds, the seventh and eight round, and the round of 64 taking place on weekends. The later rounds up to, but not including, the final, would take place on midweek evenings. The final would take place on Saturday 24 April 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.footamateur.fr/coupe-de-france-le-calendrier-complet-de-ledition-2020-2021/|title=Coupe de France. Le calendrier complet de l'édition 2020-2021|publisher=footamateur.fr|language=fr|date=24 June 2020|access-date=7 October 2020}}</ref>

On 28 October 2020, French President [[Emmanuel Macron]] announced a second [[COVID-19 pandemic in France|COVID-19]] lockdown, including the suspension of all amateur football, for four weeks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.foot-national.com/foot-foot-amateur-les-annonces-fortes-d-emmanuel-macron-142801.html|title=Foot Amateur : Les annonces fortes d'Emmanuel Macron !|publisher=foot-national.com|language=fr|date=28 October 2020}}</ref> The following day, the FFF confirmed the suspension of senior football at all levels below [[Championnat National]]. This caused the suspension of the competition, and the postponement of the sixth round and remaining fifth round matches.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.foot-national.com/foot-fff-officiel-les-championnats-et-la-coupe-de-france-s-arretent-pour-le-foot-amateur-142827.html|title=FFF : Officiel, les championnats et la coupe de France s'arrêtent pour le foot amateur|publisher=foot-national.com|language=fr|date=29 October 2020}}</ref> On 17 November, the FFF formally announced the postponement of the seventh and eighth rounds until January 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.foot-national.com/foot-coupe-de-france-le-nouveau-calendrier-de-l-edition-20202021-143749.html|title=Coupe de France : Le nouveau calendrier de l'édition 2020/2021|publisher=foot-national.com|language=fr|date=18 November 2020|access-date=18 November 2020|archive-date=18 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201118113048/https://www.foot-national.com/foot-coupe-de-france-le-nouveau-calendrier-de-l-edition-20202021-143749.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 22 December, the FFF announced a plan to resume the competition on 31 January 2021, subject to COVID-19 restrictions being removed as planned.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.footamateur.fr/coupe-de-france-la-fff-souhaite-reprendre-des-le-31-janvier/|title=Coupe de France. La FFF souhaite reprendre dès le 31 janvier|publisher=footamateur.fr|language=fr|date=22 December 2020}}</ref>

On 19 January 2021, the ''ministère des sports'' gave the go-ahead for amateur clubs involved in the competition to resume training, and the FFF produced a new calendar for the amateur path and the final stages.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://www.foot-national.com/foot-coupe-de-france-le-calendrier-de-la-competition-devoile-147201.html|title=Coupe de France : Le calendrier de la compétition dévoilé !|publisher=foot-national.com|language=fr|date=19 January 2021}}</ref>

==Notable rule changes==
Following the changes introduced regarding Guadeloupe, French Guiana and Martinique last year,<ref name=OTfootnational>{{cite web|url=http://www.foot-national.com/foot-coupe-de-france-la-revolution-pour-l-outre-mer-121206.html|title=Coupe de France : La révolution pour l'Outre-Mer|publisher=foot-national.com|language=fr|date=9 August 2019}}</ref> teams from Réunion and Mayotte also played an internal match in the seventh round. This meant an additional team qualifying for the seventh round from Mayotte.<ref name=rules>{{cite web|url=https://www.footamateur.fr/coupe-de-france-tous-les-changements-pour-ledition-2020-2021/|title=Coupe de France. Tous les changements pour l'édition 2020-2021|publisher=footamateur.fr|language=fr|date=12 June 2020}}</ref>

Ligue 2 sides joined the competition at the eighth round, a change which the FFF stated was only for this season's competition.<ref name=rules /> This meant fewer teams would qualify from each region's preliminary rounds.<ref name=rules />

Other than the final, there was no extra time in fixtures this season. Tied matches were settled by a penalty shoot-out after ninety minutes.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.foot-national.com/foot-la-revolution-coupe-de-france-divise-135992.html|title=La révolution coupe de France divise|publisher=foot-national.com|language=fr|date=30 June 2020}}</ref>

On 22 October 2020, the FFF announced that clubs from New Caledonia and Tahiti would not participate in the seventh round due to the ongoing COVID-19 situation. Two clubs were awarded byes to the eighth round. A decision was to follow on 12 November regarding other overseas teams participating in the eighth round.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.footamateur.fr/coupe-de-france-pas-de-clubs-de-nouvelle-caledonie-et-tahiti/|title=Coupe de France. Pas de clubs de Nouvelle-Calédonie et Tahiti !|publisher=footamateur.fr|language=fr|date=22 October 2020}}</ref>

On 25 November, the FFF announced that the seventh round winners from Réunion, Guadeloupe, Mayotte and French Guiana would play their eighth round matches against each other in December, rather than being integrated into the main eighth round draw when the competition restarts. The competition in Martinique would restart at the seventh round when the mainland tournament restarts.<ref name=footamnov>{{cite web|url=https://www.footamateur.fr/coupe-de-france-les-clubs-doutre-mer-saffronteront-au-huitieme-tour/|title=Coupe de France. Les clubs d'Outre-mer s'affronteront au huitième tour|publisher=footamateur.fr|language=fr|date=26 November 2020}}</ref>

On 17 December, the FFF announced a change of format to avoid cancelling the competition due to a lack of available dates. The competition would be divided into two parts: A professional path, involving teams from [[Ligue 1]] and [[Ligue 2]], and an amateur path, involving mainland teams qualifying from the preliminary rounds and the overseas qualifiers. The amateur path was straight knockout over two rounds (seventh, eighth), taking 124 qualifiers down to 31. The three overseas qualifiers re-joined the competition for the round of 64, resulting in seventeen qualifiers at the end of the path. The professional path started at the eighth round with the twenty Ligue 2 teams. The winners were then joined by the twenty Ligue 1 teams for the round of 64, resulting in fifteen qualifiers at the end of the path. The two paths joined for the Round of 32, and the rest of the competition was straight knockout.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fff.fr/article/1923-coupes-de-france-les-nouveaux-formats.html|title=Coupe de France: Les Nouveaux Formats|publisher=fff.fr|language=fr|date=17 December 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.foot-national.com/foot-coupe-de-france-la-competition-maintenue-sous-un-format-inedit-145530.html|title=Coupe de France : la compétition maintenue sous un format inédit|publisher=foot-national.com|language=fr|date=17 December 2020}}</ref>

== Seventh round ==
The seventh round was split over an extended period, starting on 21 November 2020.
* Playoff ties between teams from the overseas leagues of Guadeloupe, French Guiana and Mayotte took place between 21 and 29 November.
* The playoff tie between teams from Martinique took place on 13 January 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fff.fr/article/1930-premieres-pour-m-tsapere-et-sinnamary.html|title=Premières pour M'tsapéré et Sinnamary|publisher=FFF|language=fr|date=20 December 2020}}</ref>
* The matches involving the 124 qualifying teams from mainland France took place entirely within the regional leagues, except for those leagues providing an odd number of qualifiers, where inter-league matches were drawn. This resulted in ties between Nouvelle-Aquitaine and Occitanie, Normandy and Pays de la Loire, and Bourgogne-Franche-Comté and Paris-Île-de-France.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.footamateur.fr/coupe-de-france-le-septieme-tour-se-jouera-de-facon-regionalisee/|title=Coupe de France. Le septième tour se jouera de façon régionalisée|publisher=footamateur.fr|language=fr|date=9 January 2021}}</ref> The pre-draw was published on 22 January.<ref name=78draw>{{cite web|url=https://www.foot-national.com/foot-coupe-de-france-les-tableaux-par-regions-de-la-voie-amateur-147394.html|title=Coupe de France : les tableaux par régions de la voie amateur|publisher=foot-national.com|language=fr|date=22 January 2021}}</ref> Matches took place on 5, 6 and 7 February 2021, with three postponed to 13 and 14 February, awaiting outcomes of ties in the previous round.

== Eighth round ==
The eighth round was separated into two paths. The professional path took place between the twenty teams from [[Ligue 2]]. The amateur path took place between the 62 mainland qualifiers from the seventh round. The ties involving teams from Mayotte, Guadeloupe, Réunion and French Guiana were pre-drawn on 25 November 2020. The team from Martinique received a bye for this round and directly qualified for the round of 64 on the amateur path.<ref name=footamnov />

* Overseas ties took place on 20 December.
* The draw for the professional path took place on 7 January 2021, with matches played on 19 and 20 January.<ref name=pro8>{{cite web|url=https://www.footamateur.fr/coupe-de-france-la-fff-prevoir-le-tirage-au-sort-le-7-janvier/|title=Coupe de France. la FFF prévoit le tirage au sort le 7 janvier !|publisher=footamateur.fr|language=fr|date=30 December 2020}}</ref><ref name=8pro>{{cite web|url=https://www.foot-national.com/foot-coupe-de-france-le-tirage-au-sort-en-direct-a-17h00-146514.html|title=Coupe de France : le tirage au sort en direct à 17h00|publisher=foot-national.com|language=fr|date=7 January 2021}}</ref>
* In the amateur path, matches took place entirely within the regional leagues, with the winners of the three inter-league matches from the seventh round joining the region which had an odd number of qualifiers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.footamateur.fr/coupe-de-france-explications-en-detail-sur-le-nouveau-format-amateur/|title=Coupe de France. Explications en détail sur le nouveau format " amateur "|publisher=footamateur.fr|language=fr|date=10 January 2021}}</ref> The pre-draw was published on 22 January 2021.<ref name=78draw /> Matches took place on 13 and 14 February, with three postponed pending outcomes of ties in the previous round, and two postponed due to inclement weather.

== Round of 64 ==
The round of 64 was separated into two paths. The professional path took place between the twenty teams from [[Ligue 1]] and the ten winners of the eighth round professional path. The amateur path took place between the 31 mainland qualifiers from the eighth round and the 3 overseas qualifiers.
